From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Subject: Annual prepay: escrow sweep windows, drawdown matrix & invoice handoff

Hi Rebecca / BrightBridge team,

Thanks again for committing to the annual prepay for 2027 — excited to get this live. Attached is a proposed execution pack (RBW-2027-Annual-Prepay-Schedule.xlsx) that lays out:

- Monthly sweep windows (UTC) for drawdowns
- Milestone-triggered tranche releases (by product capacity band)
- Invoice numbering and remit instructions per country / entity
- VAT evidence checklist by jurisdiction

Two quick asks to finalize the schedule:
1) Can you confirm which legal entity and remit account you want us to invoice? If you can send a PO/PO number that matches the invoice header that avoids delays.
2) Do you prefer monthly automated ACH sweeps on the 1st of the month (we do immediate reconciliation) or milestone-triggered invoicing with a 10-business-day payment window? We can support either — the attached has both flows.

If helpful, I can lock in the sweep windows today and route the first invoice for Monday (2027-04-19) to align with your Q2 close.

Thanks,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual prepay: escrow sweep windows, drawdown matrix & invoice handoff

Hi Tessa — thanks for the pack, looks thorough. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Entity: Please invoice BrightBridge Ltd (GB entity). PO will come from Procurement and will include the PO number.
- Payment method: For 2027 we'd prefer monthly automated ACH sweeps on the 5th of each month (local bank cutoffs mean 1st is tight). Can you align the sweep window to trigger on the 5th (UTC)?
- VAT: We need the invoice to show VAT broken out by UK and EU lines; our tax team will need copies of the VAT evidence (SLA test prompts and sample logs are fine for now).
- First invoice amount: We expect the initial drawdown on 2027-04-19 per your note, but please route the first invoice to finance@brightbridge.com and cc procurement@brightbridge.com.

Also attaching the PO template — we will return it with the PO number by Friday.

One question: for tranche releases tied to usage thresholds, what is the lag between triggering and actual funds withdrawal? We want to map cashflow.

Cheers,
Rebecca

--
Rebecca Long
Head of Procurement, BrightBridge Ltd
rebecca@brightbridge.com

Kim / Marcus — looping you in to confirm operational steps once BrightBridge returns PO and confirms ACH on the 5th. Key ops items from the customer:

- Invoice header: BrightBridge Ltd (GB) — ensure GB VAT fields populated and we provide line-level VAT breakout for UK and EU.
- Sweep timing: customer requests monthly automated ACH on the 5th (UTC) instead of our default 1st. Need to confirm that doesn't collide with our bank batching / lockfile.
- Tranche lag question: customer wants lead time/cashflow mapping — we need to document the expected time from trigger to settlement.

Proposed internal play:
- Kimberly: can you confirm VAT evidence we can provide (redacted sample logs, SLA ping tests, invoice attachments) and whether finance needs any additional tax IDs?
- Marcus: can you validate that Payments queue can shift to a sweep date of the 5th for this account and estimate settlement lag (typical ACH settlement + internal posting). Also, confirm if we need to change invoice due dates to align with 10-business-day windows.

I'll reply to Rebecca once we have answers and include the final RBW invoice sample.

Thanks,
Tessa

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual prepay: escrow sweep windows, drawdown matrix & invoice handoff

Hi all — following up with operational confirmations: 

1) VAT evidence & invoice layout: We will produce an invoice with separate UK VAT and EU VAT lines. For evidence, we can provide: (a) redacted SLA trace export (sample), (b) sample prompt/response hashes used for quality checks, and (c) a signed statement of data retention policy for the account. I'll attach the redacted sample logs as soon as Rebecca confirms which EU country lines they need.

2) Sweep timing & settlement lag: Payments can be scheduled to sweep on the 5th UTC. Typical timelines: ACH initiation on the 5th -> settlement posting in 1-2 business days; internal ledger posting is same day we receive the funds (usually within 24 hours of settlement). If BrightBridge needs the invoice due date to be 10 business days post-invoice, we can set invoice_date = 1st and payment_due = 10 business days, but given their preference we'll invoice with a target collection date of the 5th and note expected posting lag in the invoice memo.

3) Tranche release lag: For usage-triggered tranche releases we operate a 48-72 hour operational buffer between trigger and drawdown to allow for batching and reconciliation. We'll document this as 'expected lag' in the drawdown matrix and include it in the invoice memo.

Next steps: Tessa — once you get the PO from Rebecca, I will send the first invoice PDF (RBW-INV-20270419-001.pdf) and a short ACH instruction text file (payment-instructions-ACH.txt) to their finance mailbox. Marcus — I'm happy to sync on ledger tagging after you confirm the sweep pipeline change.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
